newsitem.title: USA: Altera see growth slowing in third quarter.
newsitem.headline: Altera see growth slowing in third quarter.

text.p: Semiconductor maker Altera Corp said Wednesday it expects low-to-mid single digit sequential revenue growth in its September quarter due to the aggressive price reductions it announced at the end of June.

The company made the comments after a closed telephone conference call with analysts following its second quarter earnings report, in which revenues rose to $164.1 million, up 41 percent from $116.3 million in the 1996 second quarter and a 15 percent gain from the first quarter's $142.4 million.

"We expect sequential growth in the low-to-mid single digit growth rate because of these new prices which we instituted on July 2," said Thomas Nicoletti, vice president of business development and industrial relations.
"Gross margins will decline to historic levels because of these new prices," he added, noting that historic gross margins for the maker of programmable logic chips are in the 61 to 62 percent range.

The price cuts involved a reduction by up to 49 percent on its Flex 10K and MAX 7000S families of programmable logic devices, and the company said at the time it expects ongoing reducion in size of the devices to drive prices down by as much as 50 percent a year through the year 2000.

Nevertheless, Nicoletti said new products, including the Flex 10K and the MAX 7000S as well as the Flex 6000 introduced in June and the MAX 9000, accounted for 18 percent of second quarter revenues, up from 11 percent in the first quarter.

Altera, based in San Jose, Calif., earlier reported record second quarter net income of $39.7 million, or $0.40 a share on a fully diluted bases, up 64 percent from $24.3 million a year ago and up 17 percent from $34.1 million in the first quarter, ended March 31.

The per share earnings figure beat Wall Street's First Call consensus estimate of $0.39 by a penny, and compares with fully diluted earnings per share of $0.26 a year earlier and $0.35 in the March quarter, the company said.
Analysts said earnings should be roughly flat in the September quarter compared with the June quarter just ended, but they see momentum picking up in the fourth quarter.

"It looks like revenue and earnings will both be flat sequentially...in the September quarter," said UBS Securities analyst Charles Boucher, adding he was still reviewing his earnings model following the conference call.
"I think it's easily attributable to a one-quarter effect. I would expect to see growth resume in the December quarter."

Several analysts said they expect shares of the high-flying chipmaker, which reported results after the market close, to slide Thursday. Altera hit a new 52-week high of $62 in Wednesday's market rally, but closed off $1.875 at $58.
Nicoletti declined comment on earnings projections.
Robertson, Stephens analyst Dan Niles said the aggressive price cuts could hurt revenues by about three percent during a quarter which is usually slow due to summer seasonality.

"The thought is they should get back to more normal growth rates in the fourth quarter," he added, saying he had not changed his earnings per share estimates of $1.59 a share for 1997 and $2 for 1998.
